leftEvidence.role: Law, righteousness, and the inner life
leftEvidence.title: Enemy love is grounded in the Father’s generosity

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Jesus recalls neighbor love and the saying to hate an enemy, then commands love, blessing, good, and prayer toward enemies and persecutors.
points.right: Jesus commands love, good, blessing, prayer, nonretaliation, giving, and lending toward enemies.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The Father gives sun and rain to evil and good, and the hearers are called beyond reciprocal love toward perfection.
points.right: The Most High’s kindness to the unthankful and evil grounds the command to be merciful.

payload.posture: Both discourses ground enemy love in the Father’s generosity toward evil people.

rightEvidence.title: Luke ends enemy love with the Father’s mercy

payload.tension: Matthew concludes with perfection; Luke concludes with mercy, requiring source-language care.
payload.title: Perfect and merciful in enemy love
